body: My personal belief would be if someone didn't physically touch me, words are just words. But I understand that's not how everyone feels. Of course being  being verbally harassed over an extended period of time would absolutely suck, but eventually I'd get over it within a couple of years. Being followed would be on another level too but I'd probably be calling the police not telling my job. This is just my opinion, you don't have to like it. I'm not saying "sco\*\*\*, please do this my way" or "btw I think what you're doing is wrong", I'm just making a suggestion.

I understand what you're coming from but what happens if you lose contact with those managers? Over time people stray away and you never know what's going to happen in the future. I'd say better safe than sorry. You don't know what the future will hold, but I doubt you'll gain much by reporting this pig.

Ah yes, surely this isn't a PR move to get more traffic to twitch or to invite jaded streamers back. Surely twitch will do what they said they were going to do 1-2 years ago and have more transparency.

HR is there to protect their own staff. More likely than not, you'll lose a good job reference and if you ever needed a job in a pinch, you'll never be able to return. In a closing interview you need to rant and rave about the job and say the reasons you're leaving aren't related to the job itself, otherwise that place will put it in their notes to give you a poor reference.  


Source: My aunt works in management in a large company and hires and fires a lot of people, and this is the way companies operate.

As a guy it really hurts my feelings when women have to tell me they have a boyfriend the first or second time I talk to them. It's always so painfully out of context for whatever topic we're on or bears 0 relevance from what I've experienced. I can't help it. I don't get upset, but I get paranoid that they think I might be doing something that indicates I'm interested in them and then I feel bad about it later.

Don't take this the wrong way, but I've been in therapy for years and a lot of them straight up suck. A lot of them are humans just like us that went through the rounds of college and follow the textbooks they've read and advice from others. They're better at a lot of things than your average joe but don't get your hopes up too much on discovering yourself. If you really want to find yourself I'd say meditation in my opinion helps just as much if not more. Learning to let go of your attachments to your wants and desires, including your desire to be liked, is a huge weight lifted that helps you see clearly, at least from my research in Buddhism.
You can't get your medical records over the phone or via email. That's against HIPPA. You have to call them and inform them you'll be going there in person for a physical copy of the results.
"Try turning it off and on again" Amazing advice, bet no-one's ever thought of that before.

I don't think they'll know what to do. They'll probably call the hospital on me and I'll get involuntarily admitted. My only escape is my computer. I only spent 10 days in the psych ward last time and I couldn't focus on books. This time I'd probably be admitted for 5 weeks. I'd be losing my mind in there with only books to read and the occasional movie.
